content: The greatest honor you can pay to virtue is to practice it when no one is watching and no reward is promised.
author: Socrates
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Socrates understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?
